company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and based in Stanford, California. It describes its work as advancing AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition, and says its vision is to study, guide, and develop human-centered AI technologies and applications, with AI framed as collaborative, augmentative, and enhancing human productivity and quality of life. Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy are named as Denning Co-Directors. Etchemendy states that the Institute views AI as spanning the entire university and that its disciplinary expertise must be tapped to realize the technology's potential while avoiding its pitfalls.

The Institute lists fellowship and grant programs, affinity groups for students, courses for leaders and key decision-makers, specialized training for policymakers and civil servants, and work with the K-12 ecosystem, teachers, and students. It publishes an annual AI Index, which it describes as the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available and which reports a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, along with declining data transparency. Its policy work is described as evidence-based research and global convenings, and it cites the Joint California Summit on Generative AI, highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order, as focused on how the State can use generative AI to serve the people of California and on the technology's effects on the state and its workforce. Research and commentary featured on the site include Clinical Mind AI, described as a Stanford-developed international collaborative platform for clinical reasoning education through AI-simulated patient encounters; a finding that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions experience lower well-being; Erik Brynjolfsson, Director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and a Senior Fellow at Stanford HAI, arguing against the view that productivity from AI comes only by removing labor costs; and Stanford Law School researchers building an AI pipeline to comb through millions of local statutes.

No products are tracked for the Institute, and no lawsuits or MCP servers are listed. California appears as a jurisdiction of law exposure with a count of 264.
